seoTitle: Free Protobuf to Sample JSON Generator (proto3 Mapping)
metaDescription: Generate a sample JSON document from a .proto message using the canonical proto3 JSON mapping. Free, runs in your browser.
intro: Parses a .proto file (proto2 or proto3) and writes a sample JSON document for one message using the canonical proto3 JSON mapping: camelCase names, int64 as strings, bytes as base64 and enums by name.
why: Working with gRPC or protobuf APIs, you often need an example payload: for a REST gateway, a test fixture, documentation or a quick curl call. Writing JSON by hand from a message definition means remembering the mapping rules. 64-bit integers are strings, bytes are base64, enums appear by name, maps are objects, and a Timestamp is an RFC 3339 string. This tool applies those rules to your .proto source and fills in placeholder values for every field, so you get a realistic skeleton. You pick the message, or let it use the first top-level one that nothing refers to. For a oneof it outputs the first member only. The file is processed in your browser, so internal service definitions are not uploaded.
howTo: Paste the .proto source into the input box.
Optionally name the message to use, and choose camelCase field names and how 64-bit integers are written.
Copy the sample JSON and replace the placeholders with real values.

faq.q: Which JSON mapping does it follow?
faq.a: The canonical proto3 JSON mapping: lowerCamelCase names, int64 and uint64 as strings (or numbers if you choose), bytes as base64, enums by name, maps as objects and Timestamp as RFC 3339 text.
Only the first member of a oneof is included in the sample, because a real message can have only one set.
It works on the text you paste. Messages that come from imported files must be pasted in too, or they cannot be resolved.
No. They are placeholders chosen by type so the shape is correct. Replace them with realistic data for tests.
